title: Document Dedicated Burst: behavior, limits, denial reasons, and client retry guidance
author: Kira Thompson
release_notes: Adds customer-facing docs for Dedicated Burst (how it works, guardrails, and expected behaviors).
Documents denial reason codes and recommended retry/backpressure strategies.
Adds FAQ + runbook/dashboard pointers for Support/CS readiness.
description: Summary: This PR adds customer-facing documentation for the new Dedicated “Burst Capacity” option: what it is (borrowing temporary capacity from Redwood-managed burst pools), how limits/guardrails work, how to configure it (what’s controlled by Redwood vs what customers can tune), and what clients should do when burst is denied. Motivation: During beta we saw repeated support questions around (a) why burst was denied even when baseline looked “underused”, (b) what HTTP status / reason codes mean, and (c) how retries can accidentally amplify load or trigger double-counting concerns. This doc set aims to make behavior predictable and reduce time-to-resolution for incidents. Scope: Documented (1) baseline vs burst semantics, (2) per-tenant caps (max burst ratio, absolute cap), cooldown windows, and fleet safety caps at a high level, (3) denial reasons and what the platform does (fallback vs immediate backpressure), and (4) recommended client retry patterns with Retry-After handling + jitter and idempotency guidance. Non-goals: This does not document internal pool sizing policy, exact threshold numbers (these are contract/config dependent), or any cross-region bursting (not supported in initial GA). Notable behavior notes included in docs: Burst is best-effort and admission-controlled; baseline Dedicated capacity is not reduced by enabling burst. Burst is constrained to the same region and hardware class as the Dedicated baseline. When burst is denied, the platform returns a deterministic denial reason code and (when applicable) a Retry-After value; clients should not spin in tight loops. When the fleet safety circuit breaker is active, burst admissions may be broadly denied to protect non-burst SLOs. Customer guidance highlights: Prefer app-level smoothing (queues) for batch jobs; avoid synchronized retries across workers; use exponential backoff with full jitter; honor Retry-After; set an overall deadline; and ensure request idempotency keys are stable across retries. Checklists: Docs reviewed by Product + SRE; includes Support-facing “how to explain denials” section; includes example curl/SDK snippets; links to dashboards and runbook placeholders for CS enablement. Screenshots: None added in this PR (Console UI landing in a separate change); docs reference the Console location and API fields customers should expect to see. Testing: Docs build + link check in CI; manual preview in staging docs environment.
commits: docs(dedicated): add burst capacity overview + limits page
docs(api): document burst denial reason codes + HTTP behaviors
docs(guides): add retry/backpressure best practices and examples
